summary: Spore entries from the prepared 1000-title candidate queue, researched for Sami's fidelity-first archive route.

entries.title: Spore
entries.definitive_edition: Base game plus Galactic Adventures plus Creepy & Cute Parts Pack

emulation.notes: Use the current native or official release route where available.

primary.version: Spore with Galactic Adventures and Creepy & Cute Parts Pack
primary.why: The Windows PC route is the most complete route because Steam's More Spore bundle includes the base game, Galactic Adventures, and Creepy & Cute Parts Pack, and Galactic Adventures includes mission/adventure-creator content.
primary.how_to_play: Install the base game, Creepy & Cute, and Galactic Adventures on Windows, then launch through Galactic Adventures for the main run. Apply compatibility fixes/mod notes carefully and record whether online sharing features are functional.

all_releases.fidelity: Original base release family for the five-stage Spore campaign.
all_releases.reason: skip: important baseline, but incomplete versus the PC expansion/parts route.

all_releases.platform: Windows PC with Creepy & Cute Parts Pack
all_releases.fidelity: Adds creature parts, paint options, and animations.
all_releases.reason: skip: install as part of the complete PC route, not a separate playthrough.

all_releases.fidelity: Adds space-stage missions, captain progression, accessories, and Adventure Creator content.
all_releases.reason: primary: most complete official PC package when combined with base game and parts pack.

all_releases.fidelity: Spore Creatures, Spore Hero, Spore Origins and related titles are distinct spinoffs rather than ports of the PC base game.
all_releases.reason: skip: track as separate entries if queued; not secondary content for this base-game entry.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No sourced exclusive-content split requires a secondary route for this archive entry.

entries.remaster_caveats: Old online sharing/account features may be unreliable; check for compatibility fixes and note any offline-only capture limitations.
